title: Common Lime: Ancient Lindens You Can Visit
meta_description: The hybrid lime the north planted in rows. The Linde van Sambeek, 7.97 metres round, is the thickest lime in the Netherlands.
intro: Common lime is a hybrid of Europe's two wild limes, and it took over the north as the tree you plant on purpose: along canals, up drives, around squares, and in the middle of villages where decisions were made. Hilvarenbeek's aldermen read out the local decrees under theirs before the village had a noticeboard. The Linde van Sambeek is the thickest lime in the Netherlands at 7.97 metres round, hollow, with a second stem grown up inside the shell after storms took its crown in 1884 and 1901. Groningen's oldest tree is one, about 340 years old at a farmhouse called De Rollen. On a bare dike near Utrecht, boatmen on the Lek used to steer by a single lime. In Tallinn, one of the Skoone Bastion lindens was already decades old when work began on the bastion it now crowns.
